source_name: Erste Group Procurement organisational profile on LinkedIn (Procurement Services Ges.m.b.H. / s Proserv)
why_relevant: People-layer pointer: names country managing directors and sourcing specialists per market (including Romania and, by structure, the Czech entity), plus job postings that reveal category coverage and tooling. The email domain erstegroupprocurement.com identified through profile aggregators indicates a separate procurement web presence worth probing directly.

source_name: Y Soft case study — Česká spořitelna / Erste Group deployment
source_subtype: vendor case study (exemplar of a class)
why_relevant: Illustrates the general pattern that vendor-published case studies are frequently the only public record of a CZ bank award and of whether the deployment was scoped to the Czech bank or to Erste Group as a whole. As a source-class this is one of the highest-yield indirect channels for the cell.

source_name: SME Banking Club — CEE banking/payments M&A and vendor news (RBI/AKCENTA example)
why_relevant: Regional trade outlet covering CEE bank–payments transactions that split ownership between the group and the Czech subsidiary — e.g. RBI acquiring Czech FX and payments provider AKCENTA with 70% at RBI AG and 30% at Raiffeisenbank a.s. Exactly the group/subsidiary split this cell needs to detect, and reported in English only.

source_name: CaixaBank press room — CEE payments joint venture with Global Payments and Erste Group
why_relevant: Demonstrates the third-party-parent disclosure route: a CEE-wide merchant acquiring arrangement covering the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Romania (majority to Global Payments/CaixaBank, 49% Erste, HQ in Prague) was announced by the counterparty groups, not by the Czech bank. Counterparty press rooms must be monitored alongside the bank groups' own.

source_name: Byznys pro společnost — ČSOB on sustainability as a supplier-selection criterion
why_relevant: Czech CSR platform interview in which ČSOB describes how sustainability entered its tender specifications (zadávací podmínky) and became a qualitative evaluation criterion in výběrová řízení — i.e. how a KBC group policy is operationalised in Czech tender scoring. Rare local-language visibility into a bank's internal procurement criteria.

source_name: E-ZAK Ministerstvo financí ČR (contracting-authority e-procurement instance, hosts MF + resort sub-profiles)
why_relevant: Primary electronic tool and legally mandated 'profil zadavatele' of the Czech Ministry of Finance and of several resort bodies (GFŘ, SPCSS, Celní správa units). Carries full tender documentation (zadávací dokumentace), Q&A, and award records for IT/payment-related purchases that aggregators often carry only as thin metadata.

source_name: NEN – Národní elektronický nástroj, MF ČR contracting-authority profile
why_relevant: Since 1.7.2018 MF publishes procurement on its NEN profile; NEN is also the mandatory tool for many central state bodies and hosts the dynamic purchasing systems (DNS) through which state payment-gateway services are actually called off.

source_name: Platební brány pro veřejnou správu (gov.cz) – state payment-gateway programme site
why_relevant: The single most on-point source for this cell: the official programme page for payment gateways across Czech public administration. Explains that gateways are procured through a centrally-administered DNS on NEN, names the sponsoring authority and contact (platebnibrany@mvcr.cz), and describes the unified UX requirement — i.e. the demand-side rulebook payment acquirers must meet.

source_name: Architektura eGovernmentu ČR – Technická specifikace platební brány (archi.gov.cz knowledge base)
why_relevant: Publishes the technical/functional specification the state expects from payment gateways. Reading it forecasts tender requirements (supported channels, card schemes, callbacks, UX) before notices appear, and reveals which architectural bodies set the rules.

source_name: Generální finanční ředitelství – profil zadavatele (Finanční správa buying entity)
source_subtype: agency sub-profile on ministry E-ZAK instance
why_relevant: GFŘ (IČO 72080043) is the buyer for the tax administration's collection channels — card acceptance at tax offices, the MOJE daně portal payment rails, QR-payment features. Its notices are the direct signal for tax-side acquiring demand.

source_name: Celní správa ČR / Generální ředitelství cel – tender & competitive-dialogue documents (celnisprava.gov.cz)
why_relevant: Customs runs one of the largest state card-acceptance estates (a 2017 tender covered ~60 fixed plus ~84 mobile terminals) and has published competitive-dialogue minutes naming bidding banks (e.g. ČSOB). Renewal cycles of this estate are a direct acquiring opportunity signal.

source_name: Státní pokladna Centrum sdílených služeb, s.p. – profil zadavatele
why_relevant: SPCSS (IČO 03630919, VVZ profile 520646) is MF's state enterprise for data centres, cyber-security and shared services underpinning treasury systems. Its buying reveals the infrastructure layer beneath state payment rails and its own supplier bench.

source_name: Státní pokladna (statnipokladna.cz) – IISSP / RISRE programme site
why_relevant: Describes the Integrated State Treasury Information System, whose core functions explicitly include platební styk (payment transactions), plus RISRE and related modules. Establishes which systems exist, their incumbents and their lifecycle — the demand map that later tenders follow.

source_name: NKÚ – Nejvyšší kontrolní úřad, kontrolní závěry (audit conclusions)
why_relevant: State audit reports dissect how MF procured and used treasury/payment systems (licence counts, incumbent lock-in, warnings that delayed decisions will compress future tender timelines). They are the best forward indicator of an upcoming re-tender and expose contract values and supplier names.

source_name: ISVZ / NIPEZ open data on public procurement
why_relevant: Bulk machine-readable procurement data consolidating records from VVZ, NEN, Tender Arena and TENDERMARKET (new-format datasets from Feb 2024; legacy XML before that). This is the backbone for systematic, low-friction monitoring of central-state buyers by IČO and CPV rather than page scraping.

source_name: Hlídač státu – Hlídač veřejných zakázek / Hlídač smluv (+ API v2)
why_relevant: NGO aggregator that links contract register, procurement, subsidies and beneficial owners in one queryable place with a documented API — the fastest way to enumerate all contracts of a given central buyer and to snowball from buyer to supplier. Aggregation is derivative, so treat values as leads and confirm against VVZ/registr smluv.

source_name: Česká pošta, s.p. – Veřejné zakázky page and TENDER ARENA buyer profile (Z0002718)
why_relevant: Česká pošta (IČO 47114983) operates cash-in payment rails (poštovní poukázky), Czech POINT counters and is a supplier of state portal services. It buys as a sector contracting authority via TENDER ARENA, a different platform from the MF/ČNB E-ZAK world — so its notices are easily missed by MF-centric monitoring.

source_name: Portál MOJE daně / Podpora placení (Finanční správa payment channel pages)
why_relevant: Shows which payment instruments the tax administration actually offers citizens (bank transfer with variable symbol, QR payment, card where available). Changes here are the visible downstream effect of a procurement decision and give an early, low-cost signal that a gateway or acquiring contract has changed.

source_name: Věstník veřejných zakázek – vyhledání profilu zadavatele (VVZ / NIPEZ)
source_subtype: official procurement gazette / registry of buyer profiles
why_relevant: Official registry mapping every Czech contracting authority (including all kraje, statutární města, Praha and its městské části) to the URL of its profil zadavatele. This is the master index needed to enumerate the hundreds of decentralised municipal profiles where payments-related tenders actually appear.

source_name: Tender arena – profil zadavatele Hlavní město Praha
source_subtype: commercial e-procurement tool hosting a buyer profile
why_relevant: The buyer profile of the single largest municipal buyer in CZ. Prague procures city payment apps, parking payment distribution, transport ticketing, and municipal bank account/treasury services.

source_name: Tender arena – seznam profilů zadavatelů (directory)
source_subtype: buyer-profile directory on a procurement platform
why_relevant: Directory listing all buyer profiles hosted on Tender arena, including Prague, its městské části (e.g. Praha 3, Praha 10), city companies (THMP, DPP). Efficient way to enumerate one large slice of the decentralised landscape.

source_name: Portál pro vhodné uveřejnění (vhodne-uverejneni.cz) – zakázky dle sídla zadavatele
why_relevant: Hosts hundreds of municipal/regional buyer profiles and, crucially, offers browsing by seat of the contracting authority (kraj / okres / city), which lets you slice all tenders of e.g. Plzeň, Ostrava, České Budějovice without knowing each profile URL.

source_name: E-ZAKAZKY.CZ – profily zadavatelů (municipalities and Prague districts)
why_relevant: Second large commercial host of municipal buyer profiles; confirmed profiles for Statutární město Brno and Prague districts (Praha 2, 3, 19). Needed for full coverage of the fragmented profil-zadavatele landscape.

source_name: E-ZAK Moravskoslezský kraj (msk.ezak.cz)
why_relevant: Regional buyer profile of a large kraj; regions tender bank account administration/treasury services, and their subordinate organisations (schools, hospitals, transport authorities) tender POS acceptance and cashless collection.

source_name: E-ZAK Karlovarský kraj (ezak.kr-karlovarsky.cz)
why_relevant: Regional buyer profile; observed to carry financial/accounting service contracts, the same procurement family as bank-account administration and payment services.

source_name: E-ZAK Jihomoravský kraj – zakazky.krajbezkorupce.cz
source_subtype: regional E-ZAK instance with subordinate-organisation coverage
why_relevant: JMK regional profile, explicitly aggregating contracts of the region, its subordinate organisations and centrally designated suppliers — a rare case where one instance covers a whole regional family of buyers (schools, transport, social care) that buy cashless collection and POS.
